title: fix(scripts): rewrite demo imports by usage, and clear the 106 stale ones
body:
Fixes #3788

## The edge that produced the noise

`scripts/extract-mdx-demos.mjs` migrates `InteractiveDemo` / `ComponentDemo` blocks to `SchemaExample`, then swapped the page's import with one regex:

```js
/import\s*\{\s*InteractiveDemo[^}]*\}\s*from\s*['"]@\/app\/components\/ComponentDemo['"];?/
```

`\{\s*InteractiveDemo` anchors on the **first specifier** being `InteractiveDemo`. A page written `import { ComponentDemo, DemoGrid } from '@/app/components/ComponentDemo';` therefore had its content migrated and its import left exactly where it was — one dead import per migrated page, accumulated over a whole migration wave.

The rewrite now decides which named imports survive from **what the migrated file still renders**, not from one spelling of the statement. Both halves of the card are here; step 2 is the load-bearing one, since step 1 alone would refill on the next wave.

## Premise re-check on `origin/main` @ `0af9826ab`

The card estimated ~40. Re-measured, and the grading comment's numbers reproduce exactly:

| | files |
|---|---|
| import the demo module | 117 |
| statement fully dead (no name rendered) | **84** |
| one of two names dead (`ComponentDemo` gone, `DemoGrid` still rendered) | **22** |
| already clean (`SchemaExample` only, all rendered) | 11 (untouched) |

`content/docs/layout/page-header.mdx:6` verified as the live specimen the card names.

The 22 partial files are why this could not be a blanket sed: they lose `ComponentDemo` and keep `DemoGrid`. The cleanup was produced by the fixed rewriter itself, run over the tree with `ensure: []` so it is purely subtractive — it never adds an import a page did not already have.

## What counts as a use

A name is live if the page renders it as a tag **outside** fenced blocks and inline code spans. Docs pages print component tags as sample code constantly, and counting those would keep dead imports alive under a rule that reads as if it were checking usage. Renamed specifiers are judged on their **local** name.

Not in scope, and deliberately: the 84 cleaned pages mostly render `SchemaExample` without importing it, which works because `apps/site/mdx-components.tsx` provides `SchemaExample`, `DemoGrid` and `InteractiveDemo` globally. That is pre-existing and true of the 11 untouched pages too; adding 84 imports nothing needs would be the same noise in the other direction.

## Tests — `scripts/__tests__/extract-mdx-demos.test.ts` (new, 18 cases)

The script had no self-test. The new one follows this directory's convention (import the `.mjs`, types inferred through `tsconfig.scripts.json`'s `allowJs`).

The red/green pair the card asked for, on the mixed-import fixture:

- **RED** — the original regex, kept verbatim in the test as the control, leaves `import { ComponentDemo, DemoGrid } ...` sitting on the migrated page, and `ORIGINAL_IMPORT_SWAP.test(fixture)` is `false`: it never matched at all. That is what proves the spelling anchor, and not something else, was the cause.
- **GREEN** — the usage-driven rewrite prunes it.

Also pinned: all three mixed-import outcomes (none / one / both names surviving — all-or-nothing would be wrong on 22 real files); the import statement not counting as a use of what it imports; fenced and inline-code mentions not counting; local-vs-imported name on renamed specifiers; whole-tag-name matching only; `ensure` adding `SchemaExample` when the migration started rendering it and **never** adding it when unused.

Plus a ratchet over `content/docs/`, written as an **independent** scan rather than a call into the rewriter — re-running the rewriter would only assert it agrees with its own output. It catches a dead import that arrives by hand as well as one minted by the script.

## Verification

Reverse verification, direction predicted before running — **red**, and it landed on the arithmetic:

```
git checkout origin/main -- content/docs   # put the 106 stale imports back
AssertionError: expected [ ...(187) ] to deeply equal []
+   "content/docs/components/basic/button-group.mdx: ComponentDemo",
+   "content/docs/components/basic/div.mdx: ComponentDemo",
+   "content/docs/components/basic/div.mdx: DemoGrid",
```

187 = 81 fully-dead files with two names + 3 with one + 22 partial files with one. Restored, green again.

End-to-end through the real CLI on a synthetic fixture reproducing the card's miss — same input, the original script recovered with `git show origin/main:scripts/extract-mdx-demos.mjs`:

```
ORIGINAL:  import { ComponentDemo, DemoGrid } from '@/app/components/ComponentDemo';   ← stale, survived
FIXED:     import { SchemaExample } from '@/app/components/ComponentDemo';             ← pruned
```

both with the body migrated to `SchemaExample id="os3788tmp/basic-sheet"`.

Gates, all from the repo root:

```
pnpm exec vitest run scripts/              28 files, 518 tests passed
pnpm type-check:scripts                    exit 0  (both new files are in the program — verified with --listFiles)
pnpm --filter @object-ui/site types:check  fumadocs-mdx + next typegen + tsc --noEmit, exit 0
node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs           Links are valid across 7 scan roots
node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs       3969 tracked text files, OK
node scripts/check-lint-coverage.mjs       45/45 packages linted, 0 errors
pnpm exec eslint scripts/extract-mdx-demos.mjs scripts/__tests__/extract-mdx-demos.test.ts   exit 0
```

`types:check` needed `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/site^...' build` first — a fresh worktree has no `dist`, and without it tsc reports 17 `TS2307 Cannot find module '@object-ui/*'` that look like breakage and are not.

## Changeset

None owed, and the presence script arbitrates rather than my judgement:

```
$ node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs
Compared the working tree with 0af9826ab (merge-base with origin/main): 108 file(s) changed,
0 of them under the src/ of a package the release covers, 0 under a package changesets ignores,
0 changeset(s) added.
No source of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.
```

Docs and scripts only. No `skip-changeset` label — that label is not real in this repo (objectui#3724).
